appOverview: Corrector de Proyectos is a web application for FP (Formación Profesional, Spain) teachers to manage and grade end-of-cycle student projects via rubric-based scoring. It has three roles: admin (system configuration), profesor (class management and grading), and tutor (same as profesor plus panoramic grade view). The pipeline covers three academic cycles (ASR, DAW, DAM), each composed of modules. Each module has exactly one rubric, and projects belong to modules (not cycles). Grades are computed per module and then weighted by weekly hours for the final student score.

globalRules: All three user roles (admin, profesor, tutor) authenticate via username + password. Username is the Consejería de Educación system username (not email).
Default password for new accounts is '12345678'. Any user whose password is '12345678' must change it on first login before accessing the system.

Maximum 3 consecutive failed login attempts. After the 3rd failure the account is locked. A locked profesor/tutor account is unlocked by the admin; a locked admin account is unlocked by support via direct DB access.
Session auto-closes after 10 minutes of inactivity. No confirmation dialog is shown for either manual ('Salir') or automatic logout.
The student identifier (alumno.nombre) is free text. The professor may enter a real name or an anonymous code such as 'JJ499'. The system imposes no format.
All list filters are reactive: they filter as the user types, with a 300 ms debounce, without page reload.
All CRUD tables update reactively: new rows appear and deleted rows disappear without page reload.
Legislation (Legislación) is a field of the Module entity, not of the Cycle entity. The domain hierarchy is: Ciclo → Módulos (each with its own Legislación) → Proyectos → Alumnos.
A cycle stores only its name. Legislation selectors shown alongside cycle forms are navigation aids only and are not persisted to the cycle record.
The 'Año finalización' of a cycle is always displayed as start_year + 1; it is derived at render time and not stored.
A project may have 1, 2 or 3 students. The maximum of 3 is enforced at the application layer.
A student may belong to at most one project per academic year. This invariant is enforced at the database layer via trigger.
Each module has exactly one rubric. The rubric is shared across all projects of that module.
The 'Mal' level of every rubric item is always 0. This is a domain invariant enforced at both the UI and persistence layers.
The sum of all items' 'Excelente' level values in a rubric must not exceed 10 points. Adding or editing an item that would push the total above 10 is rejected with an error.
Module grades are normalised to 10: nota_módulo = (puntos_obtenidos / puntos_máximos_rúbrica) × 10, rounded to 2 decimal places.
The final student grade is a weighted average: nota_final = sum(nota_módulo × horas_semanales) / sum(horas_semanales), rounded to 2 decimal places, capped at 10.
Correction is auto-saved when the professor has selected exactly one level for every rubric item. There is no explicit 'Guardar' button for corrections.
If a correction already exists for a student+project combination, the correction screen loads the existing selection for editing.
After an auto-save, the correction screen stays active so the professor can select another project and continue correcting.
The 'Imprimir notas' button on the landing page (#47) is rendered only for users with role='tutor'. It must not appear for role='profesor'.
The PDF print button (#120) is disabled until all five cascade selects (#114–#118) have a value.
Grade status badges (#122) show green if ALL students in that module have a correction, red if at least one is missing.
Rubric file upload (#99) replaces the existing rubric entirely after a confirmation dialog. There is no partial update.
Admin can unlock blocked teacher accounts by resetting failed_login_attempts=0 and account_locked=false in the teacher record.
Delete operations on entities with dependants are always blocked with an informative error. The user must remove dependants first.
